title: What Actually Replaces Human Approval
hook: Approval and autonomy are both policies over the same consequential-action substrate.
thesis: Per the directive's own correction: the missing durable human-approval record must not be framed as a public embarrassment, because the autonomy direction intentionally removes per-action approval from ordinary authorized execution. The more interesting story is that approval and autonomy are both policies over the same consequential-action substrate: a tightly bounded autonomous envelope can execute without an approval stop, while a higher-consequence envelope can still require one. The episode shows what replaces per-action approval: constitutional invariants, policy, identity, capabilities, budgets, stable intent identity, idempotency, leases, verification, evidence, replay, watchdogs, circuit breakers, bounded adaptation, rollback. And the governing invariant: uncertainty does not become permission; if critical authority or verification disappears, new external mutations stop.

proven: The directive's correction frames approval and autonomy as policies over the same consequential-action substrate, with uncertainty failing closed (correction section).

The directive enumerates what replaces per-action approval: invariants, policy, identity, capabilities, budgets, intent identity, idempotency, leases, verification, evidence, replay, watchdogs, circuit breakers, bounded adaptation, rollback (section 8).
